note: generated by review.mjs --questions from the files named in source; never edit by hand

questions.text: Does the page's title or first line say, in one sentence, what the page is and who it is for?
Is the first thing under the title the page's core concepts, as linked icon tiles or a short list of linked items?
Does the content run in priority order, top to bottom: what it is, then its state, then what needs doing, then what was done, then detail?
rules: page: step 5, content in priority order

questions.text: Does what is still open come before what is finished?
Does the parent page's `children:` name this page, so it is reachable by clicking?
Does every view a click reaches (a tab, a selected item, an open panel) have its own URL, so a reload or the back button lands in the same place?
rules: page: creating a new page, 2; CLAUDE.md: route everything

questions.text: Does the page use a layout word or an approved type, rather than page-specific CSS for its shape?
rules: page: which kind of page is this?

questions.text: Is every item, label and button self-evident: would the owner know what it is and does without reading more?
Does every element earn its space: nothing repeats what a neighbour already shows, and no small control sits alone on a wide empty row?
Is each piece in its best form: a number or grid rather than a sentence, one filtered list rather than two lists, a structure shown rather than described?
Does every section have a title that makes the whole section clear?
rules: page: step 6; CLAUDE.md: clarity is familiar structure

questions.text: Where a working version was restructured, is the old version still reachable to compare against?
rules: page: never destroy a viable version

questions.text: Identify: which techniques does the page use? (Answer with the list, not yes or no.)
Tabs: does the tab bar fit on 1 row at 1920, at most 2 rows at 1200, and at most 3 rows at 400?
Tabs: does every tab have its own URL, so a reload lands on the same tab?
Tabs: is every tab useful, and are many tabs grouped (sub-tabs, a rail, one click down) rather than stacked into rows?
Rail or sidebar: does it sit beside a centred main column at 3440, and fold away or stack cleanly at 400?
rules: layout: defaults, navigation beside a centred main

questions.text: Rail or sidebar: does the page keep the rail and its work area still, so nothing the reader is looking at jumps when something arrives or is selected?
Bottom rail, or any fixed overlay: does the page leave room for it, so it never covers the last row of content?
rules: layout: a permanent fixed overlay owes the shell the strip it stands on

questions.text: Sheet or modal: does it have its own URL, and does closing it return to exactly where the reader was?
Full screen: is there a visible way back out, and does it have its own URL?
Does a selected item open in its own column or view, never by expanding in place and pushing the rest down?
At 3440, does the page fill the width with several columns, or a navigation column beside a centred main one, rather than one narrow column on an empty screen?
rules: layout: defaults, work at 3440 as well as 1280

questions.text: Does the page use one of the approved layouts (Standard, Split, Columns, Tile wall, Rail + content, Docs three-region), or say it is a new proposal?
For every region and box: is its width right for its content at 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440?
rules: page: step 4, how wide is it; layout: question 2

questions.text: For every region and box: does it take padding only because it needs it (a region `.pad`, a framed box `.card`, a deliberate no `.bleed`)?
rules: page: step 4, does it need padding

questions.text: For every region and box: does text keep room from every neighbour's edge and ground?
rules: page: step 4, how does it meet its neighbours

questions.text: Do two or more columns of content sit in `wide` or `bleed`, never squeezed into the reading column?
Does each band of the screen take a share that matches its importance — no band both big and nearly empty?
Do columns side by side have roughly equal content, or is a short column's hole turned into weight (centred) or spent on more content?
Is dead space answered by a new region or accepted as a gutter, never by widening a reading column past its measure?
Is content scaled to its box: nothing large in a small column, nothing tiny alone in a huge band?
rules: layout: content scale follows the box

questions.text: Does a wall of cards end on a full or balanced last row at every width, with no lone card and no reserved blank tracks?
Do flush-stacked rows share one rounded outline, and do rounded cards stand apart with a gap?
rules: layout: rounded corners and gaps go together

questions.text: Is every box auto height, with a fixed height only where content cannot grow (an icon, media of known size, a full-viewport shell, a deliberate scroll area)?
rules: layout: leave the defaults alone, height

questions.text: Are previews auto height, as tall as their content, never cropped or padded out to a fixed height?
Does every bounded box (a hero, a viewport band, an equal-height row, a scrolling rail) say what happens to longer content: scroll, clip or truncate?
rules: layout: some boxes grow, some cannot

questions.text: Is every scrollbar on the page one that was meant (a log, a code block, a rail), with no surprise scrolling box?
Is a band above the first navigation budgeted in height (`vh`), so it never pushes the navigation below the fold?
rules: layout: question 2, height above the first nav

questions.text: Does every track have a floor and a ceiling, so nothing overflows at 400 or collapses?
Do sizes meant to follow the text use `em`, and floors use `rem`?
rules: layout: leave the defaults alone; question 3, floors in rem

questions.text: Does every tab bar, title, button row and nav row sit on one line where it was meant to?
Is there no wrap that appears only under 1920 — a row that is one line at 1920 and two at 1200?
rules: measured: layout.json wraps, compared across widths

questions.text: Where a row does wrap (a control row, a chip row), is it `flex wrap` by design and does it wrap cleanly?
rules: layout: only a control row takes flex wrap

questions.text: At 400, does every full-row item stack into one column rather than crushing a track to a sliver?
rules: layout caveats: a full-row item's inside must be able to stack

questions.text: Is no preview description clipped where the same child shows at two widths (a wall card and a rail item)?
At 400, is the padding stacked at the left edge of the first heading and paragraph 3em or less?
Is no box padded inside a padded box inside a padded box, so nested levels don't add up to a big clunky block?
Is padding opted in where needed: a region `.pad`, a framed box `.card`, a deliberate no `.bleed` — and never `.pad` on a card?
rules: css: the one-line rule for which spacing word

questions.text: Does text never sit at 0 from an edge: the viewport, the nav rail, the ToC column, or any box that paints its own ground?
rules: css: text never sits at 0 from an edge

questions.text: Does every gap, pad and rhythm come from the spacing clamp (`--pad`, `--gap`, `--flow`, the `--gap-70/50/35/25` rungs), never a constant and never a multiplier?
rules: css: the padding law; layout: spacing is one knob

questions.text: Does every control (a chip, a button, a nav item) keep its own `em` padding and height, never a spacing clamp or a `vw` value?
rules: css: a spacing clamp is never the size of a control

questions.text: Does a box with padding also have a different ground, so nothing floats in midair off its siblings' margins?
Does a bled container keep `.pad` on the content inside it, so only paint touches the edge?
Is every rule inside one of the layers `base theme site util`, with no new layer name and no unlayered rule?
Is the CSS as small as it can be: an existing class, token or layout word first, no inline static styles, no class that doesn't exist?
rules: css: write as little new CSS as you can; the ladder

questions.text: Does body text reach 4.5:1 against its ground, and large text and UI shapes 3:1?
rules: layout: say the ratio out loud

questions.text: Does accent-coloured text still reach its ratio?
rules: layout: the accent is the pair most likely to fail

questions.text: Are colours tokens (`--surface`, `--wash`, `--ink`, the lighten and darken steps), never literal colours in a component?
rules: css: ownership, a token override not a new component

questions.text: Does every box meant to read as a box actually differ from its parent's ground (not `--wash` on the page, which paints nothing)?
rules: css caveats: --wash is the page ground

questions.text: Does the page work in dark mode as well as light, with `light-dark()` tokens rather than a second theme?
rules: css: ownership, light and dark are modes of one theme

questions.text: Is every seam where two grounds meet a deliberate choice, reading as one page's sections rather than two pages?
Is there one repeated anchor (an eyebrow, a coloured mark) kept identical wherever it appears?
rules: layout: repetition is the strongest tool

questions.text: Is muted text made with the `.muted` class, never `var(--muted)` as a colour?
Does the order top to bottom match priority: the most important thing is what the eye lands on first?
rules: layout: before the first factory call, focus and visual hierarchy

questions.text: Is nothing hidden off-screen: no content past the right edge, under a fixed overlay, or below an inner scroller nobody will find?
rules: layout: look at it, then cycle

questions.text: Does each box keep one rhythm (`.flow` for prose, `flex v gap` for UI), and does a wall in prose keep the prose's rhythm?
rules: layout: rhythm, one system per box

questions.text: Does each label sit clearly closer to its own card than to the next one?
Does a live page stay still as items arrive, with new items waiting behind an "N new" pill?
Does no prose line run past the measure at any width?
rules: layout: look at it, then cycle

questions.text: Is each thing shown before it is told: files as a tree, an object as its live instance, a task as its checklist, a layout as a screenshot?
rules: content: let the layout say it

questions.text: Does the layout itself show the structure (hierarchy, proximity, grouping), with no sentence spent explaining it?
rules: content: let the layout say it

questions.text: Is every paragraph 60 words or fewer?
Could the owner get the page's point in ten seconds?
Does every title say exactly what its thing is?
rules: content: words, when they earn it

questions.text: Does every picture carry at most a one-line caption?
rules: content: words, when they earn it

questions.text: Is each concept named once, the same way every time?
rules: content: name each concept once; CLAUDE.md: the same name every time

questions.text: Does every mention of a concept with its own page link to that page, and every named file or module link to its page on the site?
rules: content: connect the dots; CLAUDE.md: presentation

questions.text: Where there is a file of words (a readme, a doc, a report), does a picture or a live widget sit beside it?
rules: CLAUDE.md: show it with the widget, then use words

questions.text: Does the most important thing lead, usually the list of what this is made of, with detail one click down?
rules: content: the tip of the iceberg comes first

questions.text: Is the text written in full, plain sentences a new coder can follow, never clipped fragments or undefined jargon?
